findings.title: Fragile assertion: the new source-text oracle pins the whole `new Error(...)` expression, so a behaviour-preserving rename fails it with a message that is false
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured, not modelled. M6 renamed only the resolver's loop variable (for (const code of blockReasons) -> for (const reason of blockReasons)), leaving behaviour byte-identical; the suite went red with 'the unmapped fault lost its own name', which is false - the fault name is unchanged and only the interpolated identifier moved. The assertion over-specifies: the contract support reads is the fault NAME, and the assertion pins the name plus the template's identifier. The oracle itself is real and worth keeping - INV-05 shows it is the SOLE detector of a collapsed fault name, which is the guarantee the case's comment promises - so the fix is to narrow the assertion, not to delete it. Behavioural replacement, and it is already this file's own idiom two cases above at :269-278 (regex-extract the declaration, then assert the minimal literal): expect(source).toMatch(/throw new Error\(`unranked_auto_approval_block_reason:\$\{[^}]+\}`\)/) plus the same for the unmapped name. A bare toContain on the name alone would NOT do - both names also appear in prose inside vocabulary.ts's own docblocks, so the throw expression must stay part of the anchor. Failure mode is false-red on a harmless refactor, not false-green, which is why this is P1 rather than P0.
